title: Economic neoliberalization, inter-party competition and institutional precursors of gender-specific incarceration rates in the United States, 1981–2021
abstract: The purpose of this study is to accelerate the rise of mid-range theories of punishment (Garland 2018) by testing Wacquant’s (2009, 2010) economic explanation of mass incarceration while expanding the scope of the theory to incorporate the neglected political process of local inter-party competition. To this end, I use hierarchical multivariate linear models to simultaneously analyze women’s and men’s state-level incarceration rates in the United States as a function of labour market flexibility, welfare spending and partisan competition between 1981 and 2021. Results support Wacquant’s (2009, 2010) key thesis and show its generality, suggesting that both women’s and men’s incarceration rates are higher in the states with laissez-fair labour markets and competitive politics and are lower where labour unions are strong.
